# Requested audio: the end of every story (English)

The lines the narrator says at the end of every story in the app, in English, with their exact script and voice direction. They're the same for every story, so they're recorded once, not per story, by the same narrator as the stories: the end of a book should sound like the rest of it. **No audio in this project is generated: no text-to-speech and no voice models run in the repo or the pipeline.** Each clip is recorded or produced outside the repo and dropped into this folder, named exactly as shown.

This file is generated. To change a request, edit `content/app/narration.json` (the scripts and directions, in every language) or `content/style/voice.json` (the narrator), then run `cd tools && uv run story assets`. Run it again after delivering files, and the ⬜ entries turn ✅. Every story and language is listed in the [index](../../../../REQUESTED_AUDIO.md).

| "The End" | More endings to find | Every ending found | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0/1 | 0/1 | 0/1 | **0/3** |

- **Folder:** `content/app/audio/en/`
- **Pace:** about 115 words per minute, the slowest pace (ages 3–5): these lines close every story, for every age.
- **Script:** 3 clips, 44 words, 224 characters, about 25 s in all.

## Narrator: Warm storyteller (proposed, not yet approved)

One narrator for every English story in the app: a warm, unhurried grown-up reading a picture book aloud to a child at bedtime. Friendly, smiling and clear, never sing-song, babyish or theatrical. The same voice in every clip, so Tale Time sounds like one person reading.

- **Voice:** An adult voice with a soft, mid-range pitch and a smile in it. Clear consonants, so early readers can follow each word while it lights up on screen.
- **Delivery:** Read to one child, close by, not to a room. Keep the energy gentle and even from clip to clip: no clip should sound louder, faster or more excited than its neighbors, because the app plays them one after another.
- **Characters:** One narrator voice for everyone. Color each character's lines lightly with the personality given for them (a little quicker and prouder for a show-off, softer for a shy one), but no funny voices: they are hard to keep the same across 50 clips. A character's refrain sounds the same every time it comes back.
- **Sound words:** Read the sound words in the text (rustle, splash, hmm-mmm) playfully, as part of the reading. No sound effects, music or background: the app adds those.
- **Pauses:** A short breath of silence at each full stop and before each new speaker. In a question with two choices, a small pause before the "or", so both choices sound equally fun.
- **Pace** (words per minute; slower is better than faster): ages 3–5: 115, ages 4–7: 140, ages 7–10: 155.

**Never, in any clip:**

- Music, sound effects, ambience, reverb or room echo
- Breaths, mouth clicks, page noise or plosive pops left in the file
- A different narrator, or a noticeably different take or microphone, between clips of the same story
- Anything that isn't in the script: no clip names, page numbers, count-ins or retakes in the file
- Cloning or imitating a real person's voice (an actor, a known narrator, a celebrity) without their written permission
- Baby talk, sing-song, shouting, or scary voices for any character

## How to deliver

- **Name** each file after its clip id, in this folder: `<clip id>.wav` (or `.flac` / `.m4a`).
- **The same narrator as the stories** in this language, with the same voice, microphone and level as their clips: the app plays these right after a story's last page.
- **Packaging** turns the delivered files into mono AAC `.m4a` at about 64 kbps and evens out the loudness. Nothing else changes: no edits, no effects.
- **Licenses**: as for the stories, keep the release or license for every voice next to the files (a recorded person's written release, or a voice tool's terms that allow commercial distribution in an app).

| | Every clip |
|---|---|
| Format | WAV (preferred) or FLAC. AAC `.m4a` at 128 kbps or more only if nothing else is possible. |
| Channels | Mono. |
| Sample rate and depth | 48 kHz (44.1 kHz is fine), 24-bit (16-bit is fine). |
| Loudness | About −16 LUFS integrated, true peak at most −1 dBTP, the same level for every clip. Packaging evens out the last dB. |
| Silence | About 0.3 s before the first word and 0.5 s after the last. No fade over a word. |
| Room | Quiet and dry: no hum, hiss, echo or reverb (noise floor below about −60 dBFS). |
| Content | Exactly the script in its entry, read once, and nothing else. |

## Clips

In the order the app plays them at the end of a story: `the-end` first, then `more-endings` or `all-endings`, never both.

### ⬜ `the-end`: "The End"

- **File:** `content/app/audio/en/the-end.wav` (or `.flac` / `.m4a`)
- **When:** As "The End" rises on the ending screen, right after a story's last page.
- **Direction:** Closing the book: slowly and warmly, like the last words of a bedtime story, with a little pause after.
- **Length:** 2 words, about 2 s.
- **Script:**

> The End.

### ⬜ `more-endings`: More endings to find

- **File:** `content/app/audio/en/more-endings.wav` (or `.flac` / `.m4a`)
- **When:** After "The End", once the ending badges are out, while the story still has endings the child hasn't found: the "?" badges are those endings.
- **Direction:** An inviting, playful nudge to go and look, never a sales pitch: curious and bright on the question mark, a small pause before "And", then warm about the shelf.
- **Length:** 25 words, about 14 s.
- **Script:**

> This story has more endings to find. Tap a question mark to look for one! And there are more stories to discover on the shelf.

### ⬜ `all-endings`: Every ending found

- **File:** `content/app/audio/en/all-endings.wav` (or `.flac` / `.m4a`)
- **When:** After "The End", instead of `more-endings`, once the child has found every ending of the story.
- **Direction:** Proud and warm, a real well done for finding them all, then a gentle, happy invitation to the shelf.
- **Length:** 17 words, about 10 s.
- **Script:**

> You found every ending in this story! Now there are more stories to discover on the shelf.
